text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: Elevated 5xx rate observed for Private VPC gateway in eu-west-1. Paging on-call now: @alex (pagerduty link: https://pd.example/INC12345) :rotating_light:

alex: saw spike ~11:02 UTC, 502/504 from inference-gateway -> backend VPC. Customer reports timeouts. Pulling dashboards now.

maria: I'm on metrics. p50 latency fine but 5xx jump from 0.3% -> 18% starting 11:01. Errors grouped around gw-proxy-3 and peering-route.

sre-lead: alex, what's customer impact? any active requests failing?

alex: support-eric reported some customers hitting retry storms. Support says Acme Analytics reports dozens of failed inferences.

support-eric: confirming — customer seeing 504s in their logs and we see increased retries from their SDK. They've opened a ticket.

oncall-bot: oncall handoff: @alex -> @maria in 30m if not resolved.

maria: running quick checks: NAT ephemeral usage on transit gateway looks high. `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces` shows high ephemeral allocations.

network-eng: jumping in. Could be ephemeral port depletion on the NAT or SNAT collisions across peered accounts. Any recent deploys to private route tables?

alex: no deploys to routing in last 2 hrs. Last config change was SG update yesterday.

ops-jordan: I grabbed tcpdump from gw-proxy-3 for 10s: lots of SYN retransmits to backend hosts, then RST. suspect asymmetric path or conntrack overflow on peering appliance. snippet:
```
11:03:12.123 IP gw-proxy-3 > backend-10.2.0.15: Flags [S], seq 0, win 29200
11:03:12.456 IP backend-10.2.0.15 > gw-proxy-3: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```

maria: matches NAT metrics: SNAT sessions climbed to 64k (threshold 65k). If sessions hit ephemeral cap, new connections get dropped -> 5xx/timeouts.

sre-lead: mitigation options: 1) increase NAT ephemeral port pool on transit appliance (if safe) 2) failover traffic to fallback region/replica 3) temporary client throttling via proxy to reduce new connections.

alex: can we confirm peering flaps? route table shows intermittent flaps at 11:01-11:04. Might be peering appliance causing asymmetric SNAT.

network-eng: I see control-plane logs indicating a peering reconvergence event at 11:01 triggered by route-reflector bounce. Looks like one transit node briefly lost bgp session -> re-originated routes -> SNAT mapping inconsistent for a few seconds. That coincided with high connection churn from a customer test job.

ops-jordan: starting mitigation: applying temporary rate-limit rule on gw-proxy-*. `istio` envoy filter to cap newConn/sec from public frontends to 2000. Pushing now.

maria: pushed rate-limit to prod (gw-proxy-1..4). Observing drop in new connections, 5xx rate falling from 18% -> 6% over 60s.

support-eric: telling Acme we're throttling briefly to stabilize and asking them to pause batch jobs. They're ok for now, want ETA.

sre-lead: next step to remove single points: increase SNAT table size on transit appliance. network-eng can you change ephemeral range + restart nat-daemon? expected disruption?

network-eng: we can increase SNAT ephemeral port range from default 32k -> 64k and restart nat-daemon on transit nodes. Restart is rolling with conntrack persistence, should be low-impact but will cause short retries. Request approval.

alex: +1, go ahead with rolling restarts, coordinate with ops-jordan.

network-eng: executing now on transit-1. Command:
```
ssh transit-1
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535"
sudo systemctl restart nat-daemon
```

ops-jordan: rolling restarts started: transit-1 -> transit-2 -> transit-3. Monitoring conntrack and 5xx.

maria: 5xx dropped to 2.1% after transit-2 restart. Conntrack frees up. TTLs stabilizing.

oncall-bot: INC12345 updated: mitigation applied, monitoring for 30m.

support-eric: Acme confirms failures stopped after our throttling and restart. They're asking for RCA and permanent fix.

sre-lead: immediate mitigation done. For root cause: route-reflector flapped, caused transient peering reconvergence, high client connection churn plus limited SNAT pool -> connection drops. Action items: increase SNAT pool by default, add conntrack autoscaling, harden BGP sessions, and add proactive alert for SNAT session % usage.

alex: logging action items in incident board and tagging network team. Will schedule postmortem tomorrow.

network-eng: filing follow-ups: add guardrail to prevent route-reflector restarts during peak, implement conntrack autoscale on transit appliance, and add end-to-end test to simulate peering reconverge.

ops-jordan: handing off to daytime on-call @sre-lead for next 2h monitoring. If 5xx stays <1% and Acme OK, we resolve.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete: @ops-jordan -> @sre-lead.

sre-lead: thanks team. Good run. I'll own the postmortem and customer comms.

maria: saving logs and dashboards, will attach to PM.

alex: closing loop: temporary throttles removed, transit SNAT range persisted, monitoring alerts tuned. Keep eyes open for similar spikes. :thumbsup:
